name: The Notorious B.I.G.
hook: A Brooklyn rapper whose debut was steered from street records towards radio hits by Sean Combs, with one of its hardest tracks by DJ Premier, and whose murder in 1997 is still unsolved.

blurb.age13: Christopher Wallace, the Notorious B.I.G. or Biggie Smalls, was born in Brooklyn in 1972 and grew up in Clinton Hill. Sean Combs heard his demo tape and signed him to Bad Boy Records in 1993. His first album, 'Ready to Die' (1994), had dark, detailed songs about crime and poverty, and also radio hits like 'Juicy', built on a sample of Mtume's 'Juicy Fruit', which Combs pushed him to make. DJ Premier produced 'Unbelievable'. He became caught up in a feud with his former friend Tupac Shakur, which grew into a rivalry between East Coast and West Coast rap. Tupac was shot dead in September 1996. In March 1997 Biggie was shot dead in Los Angeles, aged 24. Nobody has been convicted of either killing. His second album came out two weeks after he died.
blurb.adult: Born on 21 May 1972 in Brooklyn and raised in Clinton Hill. Sean Combs signed him to Bad Boy in 1993. 'Ready to Die' (13 September 1994), recorded at the Hit Factory and D&D Studios in 1993 and 1994, mixes the darker early sessions with radio singles, 'Juicy' (on Mtume's 'Juicy Fruit') and 'Big Poppa', that came from Combs's encouragement in the later sessions; DJ Premier produced 'Unbelievable', and Easy Mo Bee and others most of the rest. From 1995 he was in a feud with Tupac Shakur, a former friend, that became the centre of the East Coast and West Coast rivalry. Shakur was shot dead in Las Vegas in September 1996. Wallace was killed in a drive-by shooting in Los Angeles on 9 March 1997, aged 24; the murder is unsolved. 'Life After Death' came out on 25 March 1997 and debuted at number one.
